structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single candidate architecture/design document for the Pre-Python gate at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/conformance-and-sovereignty.md, limited to documentation and local packet/readiness evidence, defining Node-to-Python coexistence/conformance strategy and Python Sovereignty acceptance criteria without implementing Python or changing source/test/config/runtime state.
structuredContent.summary: The supplied packet provides sufficient governing authority, scope limits, source baselines, acceptance criteria, exclusions, and verification expectations to draft one reviewable candidate design artifact. The work is cohesive: G33 coexistence/conformance and G34 sovereignty criteria are tightly coupled parts of the same migration gate. Remaining uncertainty is primarily engineering/document-research work, not unresolved owner intent.
implementation_unknowns: Exact retained Node invariants and adapter accidents must be extracted and mapped from the cited Node source/test/evidence material without independently verifying content in this assessment.
The candidate document must determine how to present successful and failing behavioral scenarios traceably against Authority §§42–43, Node evidence, B-DISP records, and EOS constraints.
The author must distinguish binding authority from candidate EOS/source material, especially where EOS source is only a candidate conformance pin and not blanket adoption.
The document must identify any unresolved Founder decisions encountered during drafting rather than resolving material architecture/security/storage/product choices itself.
The local packet/readiness evidence paths and documentation checker expectations must be aligned with the repository’s existing documentation conventions.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable as a document review: the candidate artifact can be checked for path/scope compliance, traceable source/invariant mapping, explicit contract semantics with successful and failing examples, conformance/coexistence coverage, Python Sovereignty proof requirements, rollback/retirement authority, labeled candidate semantics, exclusions from implementation, and recorded unresolved Founder decisions. One independent content review against the supplied authority rows and cited source categories is meaningful because the output is a single bounded design artifact with local evidence, not a runtime change requiring distributed operational validation.
material_risks: The drafter may accidentally convert candidate design language into asserted Founder-approved architecture or API stability claims.
The drafter may overfit to Node implementation accidents instead of separating retained behavioral invariants from adapter-specific details.
The drafter may silently resolve material Founder decisions that should instead be recorded as unresolved candidate choices requiring review.
The drafter may imply Python capability proof from historical Node-only evidence, which the packet explicitly forbids.
The drafter may exceed scope by editing neighboring architecture documents, EOS material, source, tests, configuration, services, profiles, secrets, or implementation artifacts.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the single candidate design document and its local packet/readiness evidence within the authorized documentation scope, using the supplied authority and evidence categories, and stop only if a concrete material Founder decision prevents candidate drafting.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the owner has clearly authorized documentation-only work, named the intended artifact, bounded writable areas, provided governing architecture authority and gate criteria, specified acceptance and verification expectations, and explicitly stated how to handle unresolved material decisions. The work does not contain materially independent decision centers requiring semantic splitting; G33 and G34 are interdependent aspects of one Node-to-Python migration gate. No external prerequisite is established as unavailable, and ordinary research into the cited local sources is an implementation/document-authoring unknown rather than a reason to clarify intent.
